subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What different aspects of their purchase are Amazon reviewers actually talking about?

judge.implied_focus: Aspects/topics of the purchase experience that Amazon reviewers discuss

per_column.name: competitor_or_alternative_comparison
per_column.rationale: Whether the review compares to competitors/alternatives is a legitimate single aspect reviewers talk about, so it aligns with the aspect-decomposition focus. However, it is only ONE facet and does not constitute a structured set of aspects.

judge.rationale: The query asks for the DIFFERENT aspects reviewers discuss, implying a multi-facet decomposition (e.g., price, quality, shipping, usability, customer service, comparison). Only a single boolean aspect column was added. With just one facet there is no way to assess coherence across multiple columns, and the structure is essentially a single restatement of one dimension rather than a differentiated aspect set. It centres on a plausible aspect (so focus is coherent-ish), but it fails structure_quality because a single boolean cannot represent the range of 'different aspects' requested, and actionability is limited since an analyst learns only comparison presence, not the spread of topics.
